To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) GDA converges globally in the hidden mapping geometry; (2) in the case of Fisher geometry, GDA has a fixed point that is a saddle point and the dynamics are invariant to a certain class of transformations; and (3) the dynamics in the Fisher geometry can be completely characterized in the special case of team competition.

(i) GDA converges to a Nash equilibrium in Hidden Convex Concave Games under mild assumptions, and (ii) GDA convergences to a Nash equilibrium when the players have access to the Fisher Information matrix in the case of team competition.

(i) in Hidden Convex-concave games the GDA flow is globally convergent and (ii) in GANs the GDA flow in Fisher geometry is globally convergent in team competition and is a gradient flow on a manifold in the non-team competition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions: (i) What are the properties of the generalized Gradient Descentralized Ascent (GDA)-flow in Hidden Convex Concave Games? (ii) How does the geometry of the game affect the dynamics of GDA?
two main themes: (i) developing a theory of GDA in a large and important class of non- convex non-concave games and (ii) providing a complete understanding of the GAN dynamics in a special case.
the following questions: What is the geometry of Hidden Convex-Convex games? What are their dynamics? What is the role of the Fisher geometry?
